method.evidence_tree: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
method.scope_discipline: Worked only from the exported data/ cache and docs/math-foundations.md. Did not read src/, tests/, scripts/, docs/plans/, docs/receipts/, the diff, or git history. The scenario definition and the golden baseline live in scripts/ (out of scope), so the fight setup was NOT observed; the verdict is derived from the ratio between the two values and the cached wiki rules that can produce it.

sources_quoted.quote: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.

{{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.

Independent damage value modifiers distinct from resistances: percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.
every damage event carries one damage type (physical/magic/true)
m(R) = 100 / (100 + R) (apply_resistance, resistance.py) ... mitigation commutes with expectation (linear in raw)

sources_quoted.source: data/atoms/autoresearch-review.md, line 95 (establishes what a 'pair' is in this engine)
sources_quoted.quote: each pair fight cannot see the roster, so the engine authors the full value with an explicit reduced receipt; the coupled ledger re-prices defenders past the first

step_1_identify_the_factor.note: The two values differ by exactly one multiplicative factor of 1.12, to within 1-decimal-place display rounding.

step_2_round_trip.conclusion: The change is exactly the removal (or de-duplication) of one Abyssal Mask 'Unmake' curse factor of +12%.

step_3_rule_out_other_factors.imperial_mandate_command: 1.07 (Vulnerable, all damage types). 225.6 x 1.07 = 241.4 != 252.7, and 225.6 x 1.07 x 1.12 = 270.4 != 252.7. The 7% Mandate factor alone cannot produce the delta; it is unchanged by this diff (present in, or absent from, both values identically).
step_3_rule_out_other_factors.resistance_mitigation: Under m(R) = 100/(100+R) a 1.12x swing would require the target's post-penetration resistance to move from R to 1.12*(100+R)-100 (e.g. 45.6 -> 63.1). No cached Abyssal/Mandate value produces such a resistance change: Abyssal Mask's 45 MR is granted to its *holder*, not to the enemy, and neither item carries magic penetration or MR shred. Coincidence with the literal cached '12' of Unmake is implausible.
step_3_rule_out_other_factors.crit_or_proc_counting: Discrete counting changes (renewal counts N(T) = floor(AS*u*T), modular every-Nth procs -- docs/math-foundations.md 1.1/1.2) move a total by an integer multiple of a hit, not by a clean 12.0% of the value. Rejected.

step_4_what_the_wiki_permits.unique_and_type_gated: Unmake is a unique passive on a single legendary item and its amplification is explicitly scoped to MAGIC damage ('12% increased magic damage', 'take 12% more magic damage'). Therefore, for any single damage event, the only legitimate Unmake contribution is a factor of exactly 1.12 (event is magic damage AND the cursed target is in range) or exactly 1.00 (event is physical or true damage). A factor of 1.12^2 = 1.2544 is never legitimate: the item cannot be duplicated and a second holder's curse does not stack a second instance onto the same debuff.
step_4_what_the_wiki_permits.consequence: Old = New x 1.12 means the old ledger carried exactly one MORE Unmake factor than the new one. Only two arrangements are consistent with the cached text: (a) old applied Unmake to a non-magic (physical/true) event and new correctly gates it to magic damage; or (b) old applied Unmake twice to a magic event and new correctly applies it once. In both arrangements the NEW value is the wiki-correct one.

step_5_the_only_old_correct_path_and_why.path: The old value would be correct only if event 27 is genuinely magic damage against a cursed target and the change wrongly stripped a legitimate +12%.
why_rejected: The 'pair' in pair_damage is the engine's roster-blind pair fight (data/atoms/autoresearch-review.md: 'each pair fight cannot see the roster'). A pair fight therefore cannot pick up an ALLY-held Abyssal Mask in the first place, so the removed factor cannot be an ally-aura contribution that the change wrongly discarded; it must have come from the attacker's own loadout, where it is either legitimately applied once (and a second copy is a double-count) or illegitimately applied to a non-magic event.
Nothing in the cached text creates a condition under which a self-held Unmake stops amplifying the holder's own magic damage, so a 'lost legitimate amp' story has no source support.

Conversely, the cached text carries an explicit, easy-to-miss type gate ('magic damage') that Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable (7%, 'from all sources', all damage types) does NOT carry. A scenario that pairs these two items is precisely a test of that contrast, and an over-broad curse applied to physical/true events is the failure mode the gate exists to prevent.

step_6_result.identity: pair_damage = base_post_mitigation x (1.07 if Vulnerable else 1.00) x (1.12 if magic AND cursed else 1.00), factors multiplicative per data/wiki-atoms/damage.json 'damage.modifier'
step_6_result.implied_pre_curse_base: 225.6 (already carrying any Mandate/mitigation factors, which are identical in both values)

limitations: The scenario definition (champions, items, roster, ability ranks) and the golden baseline live in scripts/, which runbook R-18/R-19 places out of scope, so the damage TYPE of combat/events[27] could not be read directly. The verdict is therefore inferred from the exact 1.12 factor plus the cached Unmake rule, not from a full end-to-end re-simulation of the event.

Both admissible readings of the delta (magic-only type gate; de-duplication of a double-applied curse) converge on the same verdict, which is what carries the confidence; a re-simulation would be needed to say WHICH of the two it is.
